title: Scanning a true prefix
statement: Let $M$ be a Turing machine with no work tapes, let $q$ be a state, and let $e$ be a Boolean bit. Suppose that whenever the input symbol is true, every work-tape reading gives a transition that moves the input head right, emits false if $e$ is true and emits nothing if $e$ is false, and remains in state $q$. For every Boolean word $x$ and every $j\le |x|$ such that the first $j$ entries of $x$ are all true, after $j$ steps from the scan configuration at position zero in state $q$ with empty output, the machine is in state $q$ at position $j$; its output is the word of $j$ false entries if $e$ is true, and is empty if $e$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: The transition condition holds for every work-tape reading on input true
The first $j$ entries of $x$ are all true
